intuition.title: Proposed precursor network
intuition.summary: At 320–350 °C viscosity and apparent boiling point rise; low-temperature complex signals later disappear near nucleation. The authors propose a cross-linked iron-oleate network that breaks down while releasing FeO monomers. Mechanistic proposal; no unique direct molecular structure of the network established.
intuition.scope: Mechanistic proposal; no unique direct molecular structure of the network established.

intuition.title: Star-to-cube growth
intuition.summary: Fast anisotropic star growth is followed by smoothing/truncation, then a slower cubic growth regime attributed to Ostwald ripening. Morphology-based growth interpretation; no independently measured monomer count or diffusion constant.
intuition.scope: Morphology-based growth interpretation; no independently measured monomer count or diffusion constant.

scopeLabel: Distinct route; source-defined variants and specimens remain separate.

general_background.title: Conversion of a precursor
general_background.summary: Thermal decomposition changes a precursor into species available for further reaction or growth. Bond cleavage and ligand transformations can change the supply of growth species, with competing pathways set by the precursor and medium.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
